venue.name: Government House (Lieutenant Governor of BC)
venue.description: Government House is the office and official residence of the Lieutenant Governor of British Columbia and, in the site's words, the ceremonial home of all British Columbians. It stands in the Rockland neighbourhood of Victoria, on the traditional territory of the Songhees and Esquimalt First Nations. The house is open to the public through free guided tours for which pre-registration is required, and small private group tours can be booked on weekdays by non-profit, community or academic organizations such as schools. The grounds and gardens, which include more than twenty named gardens, a duck pond, an orchard, a bandshell and a Garry oak woodland with a marked trail, are open to the public 365 days a year and are free to visit; a printable scavenger hunt map is published for exploring them. On the estate, the Cary Castle Mews houses a seasonal Costume Museum and Rudi's Tea Room.
venue.address: 1401 Rockland Avenue, Victoria BC V8S IV9

facility_notes.lunch_space: If you would like refreshments, we invite you to visit the Cary Castle Mews Tea House located on the Government House grounds, open May through September.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Public tours include stairs, walking, and standing in place. There is minimal seating available. There is no access to elevators but a ramp is available for wheelchairs, walkers, etc.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is ample free parking in the Lower Lot (located at the Cary Castle Mews) and in front of Government House. Please note parking is no longer available near the Bandshell in order to protect the root systems of nearby trees.

restrictions: Government House does not take bookings for space usage. Formal ceremonies, such as weddings or celebrations of life, are not permitted to take place on site.

Government House does not permit the importation and use of outside furniture; this includes barbeques and propane fire pits. The only exceptions are for portable/collapsible chairs that are not affixed to the ground or structure.
Bicycles are not permitted for riding on walking paths or lawns.
Any amplified sound and/or other noise that may disturb or impede the enjoyment of visiting patrons or neighbours is not permitted.
Dogs are welcome and must be on leash.
Highly poisonous death cap mushrooms may be found on the property. Use caution with children and pets, and please do not touch or pick any mushrooms on the grounds, for safety.
In accordance to Clean Air Bylaw No. 3962 it is prohibited to burn or vape any substances, including cannabis, on the public grounds of Government House.
No organization may sell tickets or access to a private group tour.
venue.hours_notes: During the spring and summer, the Government House grounds are open from 5:30 am until 9:00 pm. The grounds and gardens are open to the public 365 days a year, and are free to visit.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Costume Museum in the Cary Castle Mews and Rudi's Tea Room both open for the 2026 season on Tuesday May 19 and close on Friday August 28, running Tuesday to Friday. Published special closure dates are June 30 and July 1 for both, plus August 4-7 for the Tea Room.
venue.price_year_or_season: 2026 season dates and menu published for the Costume Museum and Rudi's Tea Room

programs.name: Private group tour
programs.description: Small group tours for non-profit, community, or academic organizations (such as schools) can be booked during weekdays. Tours are one hour, between 10:00 am and 3:00 pm on weekdays only, and are subject to availability. Booking is by a request form on the Tours page which asks for the organization, contact details, number of attendees, the group's knowledge of English, any mobility challenges, a description of the organization, and up to three preferred dates with a start time chosen from 10:00 am, 11:00 am, 1:15 pm and 2:00 pm. Tours are only conducted in English, and no organization may sell tickets or access to a private group tour. The page does not say whether a private group tour is free.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the rooms of the Lieutenant Governor's official residence with a guide, standing and listening while the guide talks about the building's history, its art and its architecture.
programs.our_note: An hour on your feet with stairs and almost nowhere to sit - hard going for under-fives, and the form asks up front about mobility needs, so say so there. The site never states a price for the private version even though public tours are free, so confirm that when you submit the form, along with where the group can eat and use a washroom.
programs.practical_summary: One hour on weekdays at a fixed start time, in English only, booked through a form with no stated notice period. Cost, washrooms, indoor lunch space, group size limits and any minimum age are all unstated - the only facility detail published is free parking and a ramp in place of an elevator.
programs.evidence: Small group tours for non-profit, community, or academic organizations (such as schools) can be booked during weekdays.

programs.name: Public guided tour
programs.description: Government House is open to the public via free guided tours covering history, points of interest, and art and architecture. Space is limited and visitors must register in advance through the Government House Eventbrite page, up to two weeks ahead. As of the September 2026 reading, the page says there were limited dates in August because of events at Government House and that there will be regular Saturday tours in September. The site notes that public tours are limited to individual registrants, so a group leader would use the private group tour route instead. Tours include stairs, walking and standing in place, with minimal seating; there is no access to elevators, but a ramp is available for wheelchairs and walkers.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the residence's public rooms on foot, standing to look at the art, the architecture and the objects the guide points out.
programs.our_note: Free, but tickets are released to individuals rather than groups, so this is not a way to get a class in - use the private group tour form for that. The Saturday timing suits a family recommendation more than a weekday outing.
programs.practical_summary: Free and pre-registered through Eventbrite, on Saturdays, with stairs, standing and minimal seating. Tour length, minimum age and washroom or lunch arrangements are not published.
programs.evidence: Tours are free but space is limited, and visitors must register in advance.

programs.name: Self-guided grounds and gardens visit
programs.description: The grounds and gardens are open to the public 365 days a year and are free to visit, with no booking. During the spring and summer they are open from 5:30 am until 9:00 pm. The site publishes a free downloadable Scavenger Hunt map of the estate with fifteen numbered stops, covering the ceremonial front gates and the coat of arms, the duck pond, the bandshell, the orchard, the Hosaqami totem pole, the sunken Rose Garden statue, the Dawn Redwood, the Woodlands viewpoint and trail, the Cary Castle Mews and the Chauffeur's Cottage, with answers printed on the map. There is ample free parking in the Lower Lot at the Cary Castle Mews and in front of Government House. The estate rules apply, including a warning that highly poisonous death cap mushrooms may be found on the property.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the garden paths and the Woodlands Trail with the printed scavenger hunt, counting the ducks on the pond, the salmon carved on the bandshell, the orchard trees and the flags flying, and hunting for the stone statue in the sunken Rose Garden and the totem pole.
programs.our_note: This is the part of the estate that works for young children: free, open every day, no booking, and the scavenger hunt gives them something to do rather than something to be shown. Print it before you leave - it is a PDF on the site, not a handout at a desk. Brief the group about not touching mushrooms; the site's death cap warning is specific about children.
programs.practical_summary: Free, open 365 days a year with free on-site parking, and no booking needed. No washroom, picnic area or shelter is described anywhere on the site, and the only refreshments mentioned are the seasonal tea room, so plan toilets and lunch elsewhere.
programs.evidence: The grounds and gardens are open to the public 365 days a year, and are free to visit.

programs.name: Costume Museum visit
programs.description: The Costume Museum is located in the Cary Castle Mews, by the lower parking lot, in a cluster of 19th century wooden service buildings that includes stables, a carriage house, a gaol, a root cellar, a wash house and a poultry house. With changing displays every year, it tells the story of Lieutenant Governors and the history of Victoria and British Columbia through fashion, showing some of more than 200 costumes from the 1860s to the 1970s along with vintage accessories, period artifacts and Government House memorabilia; the site says docents are on hand to explain the displays. For 2026 it opened on May 19 and closes on Friday August 28, open Tuesday to Friday 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, with special closures on June 30 and July 1. No admission price and no group booking route are published for the museum.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the old stable buildings looking at gowns, accessories and objects from Government House, with docents there to answer questions.
programs.our_note: Short season and weekdays only, and it closes at the end of August - by the time school starts it is shut for the year, so this is a spring or summer outing for a daycare rather than a September class trip. Nothing says whether groups can be accommodated or whether it costs anything, so ask.
programs.practical_summary: Open Tuesday to Friday, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, from mid-May to the end of August only, beside the lower parking lot. Admission price, group booking, capacity and any facilities are not published.
programs.evidence: The Costume Museum is located in the Cary Castle Mews, lower parking lot.

gaps: No price is published for private group tours. Public tours are stated to be free and the grounds are stated to be free, but the private group tour section says nothing about cost, so it is left null.
No minimum or maximum group size is published for private group tours; the request form asks for the number of attendees but sets no limit, and the copy says only "small group tours".
No minimum notice period (lead time) is published for a private group tour, and no cancellation or confirmation policy is stated.

No minimum age, age range or grade range is published for any tour, so age_basis is null on every program. Whether the house tour suits under-fives is not addressed beyond the note that tours involve stairs, walking and standing with minimal seating.

The booking email is hidden behind Cloudflare email protection on the General Enquiries page and could not be read. No booking phone is published either; the page gives 250-387-2080 for questions about the grounds and correspondence, 250-387-2079 for security after hours, and fax 250-387-2078.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site, for the house, the Mews or the grounds.
No indoor lunch space or picnic area is described. The only food on site is Rudi's Tea Room, a seasonal café with first-come, first-served seating and no reservations.
No rain backup is described for a grounds visit.

Stroller access is not addressed. Wheelchair access is only partly answered: public tours include stairs and standing, there is no elevator, and a ramp is available - so the boolean is left null with the wording kept in facility_notes.
Bus or coach parking is not addressed; the site says only that there is ample free parking in the Lower Lot and in front of Government House.
The postal code is published on the site as "V8S IV9", with letters where digits are expected; the address is recorded as the site writes it and should be corrected before it is used for post.

Guided garden tours are offered by The Friends of Government House Gardens Society, and Government House links to fghgs.ca for tour details, cost and booking. That is a separate organisation's site, so nothing about those tours has been extracted here.

The Tours page states the public tour schedule in relative terms ("limited dates available in August", "regular Saturday tours in September") without listing dates, and the dates themselves live on Eventbrite, off the venue's domain.

Neither image on the site carries an alt attribute; both alt texts here were written from the file names and the surrounding page text, without viewing the files. Photographs elsewhere on the site sit in JS-driven sliders that did not render in the fetched markup.
